- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- If sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, model frequently fails to adjust downward; reduce forecast slope in the 2nd half of the 30-day window.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2–3% per day until convergence.
- Model underestimates true volatility when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 1–2% upward bias in early forecast days if sentiment > 0.0.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overweights recent 7–14d data; reduce weight of last 7 days if sentiment is negative or volatile.
